title_ar: الشيخ الددو.. يجيب على بعض الأسئلة الواردة للموقع..
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Answers a Number of the Questions Sent to the Site
body_ar:
في إطار خدمة "الفتاوى" التي يقدمها الموقع العلمي لفضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو، وردت إلى "بريد" الموقع عدة أسئلة متنوعة ، أجاب عليها فضيلة الشيخ كتابة.

وتشمل هذه الطائفة من الأسئلة ، مواضيع متنوعة ، حيث اشتملت على أسئلة في الأخلاق والمعاملات والاقتصاد ، والفرق والجماعات الإسلامية ، و أحكام الرؤية بالنسبة المقيمين في غير بلادهم.

نص الأسئلة والاجوبة :

السؤال الأول:

السلام عليكم شخنا ....

أعلم أن الغيبة محرمة ومن الكبائر ولكن هل كلما أردت السؤال عن الناس ومعرفة أحوالهم وما يجره من التفاصيل ، غيبة ؟؟

أصبحت أوسوس في ذلك ؟ وماذا عن حديث عائشة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ام زرع والكلام في أزواج النسوة من أحكام ؟؟

أتمنى أن يكون هناك حكم يريحني ويبعدني عن العزلة.

الجواب على السؤال 1 )

الجواب على السؤال الأول: أن الوساوس من خطوات الشيطان التي نهى الله عن اتباعها فقال تعالى: ( يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر) وقد عرف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الغيبة بقوله: (هي ذكرك أخاك بما يكره) فإذا كان الإنسان غائبا فاستطال في عرضه

لينقصه ويبخسه فتلك الغيبة التي حرم الله سواء تعلق ذلك بخلْق أو خُلُق أو غيرهما ولا يدخل فيها السؤال عن أحوال الناس لكن ينبغي للسائل عن أحوال الناس أن يقتصد ويقتصر على ما يعنيه فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :( من حسن إسلام المرء تركه ما لا يعنيه) وحديث أم زرع المذكور ليس من باب الغيبة بل من باب التشكي والذي يقصد به التخفيف والمواساة كما قال الشاعر:

فلا بد من شكوى إلى ذي مروءة * يواسيك أو يسليك أو يتوجع.

وقد ذكر أهل العلم ما استثني من تحريم الغيبة فعدوا منه ما تعلق بالجرح والتعديل في الرواية وفي النصيحة وما جاهر به صاحبه وأعلنه مما هو محرم شرعا وما يذكر به أهل البلدان مما هو شائع فيهم وما يتذاكره اثنان مما هو معلوم لكل واحد منهما.

والله أعلم.

السؤال الثاني : هو أنني أريد البحث في المذاهب الضالة وتفرعها ومعتقداتها بشكل مبسط وشامل فما الكتب التي تتحدث في ذلك ؟ وهل كثرة الأحزاب والجماعات الإسلامية ومنها السلفية والاخوان وغيرها خيرا للأمة ؟ وما السبيل حتى لا تفترق الأمة إلى ثلاث وسبعين فرقة ؟ أتمنى أن يكون سؤالي واضحا وبارك الله فيكم.

الجواب على السؤال الثاني: حديث افتراق الأمة قد ورد من طرق متعددة لا تصح منها واحدة وقد صححه بعض أهل العلم بطرقه ومتابعاته وشواهده غير أن ذلك لا يصحح أطرافه وإنما يمكن به تصحيح الأصل فقط . فلا يصح ( كلها في النار إلا واحدة) أو ( كلها في الجنة إلا واحدة) أو ( من كان على مثل ما أنا عليه أنا وأصحابي) ، وعلى فرض صحة أصل الحديث فهو خبر عن أمر غيبي لا يلزم السعي لتحصيله والمقصود به فرق المنحرفين في اعتقادهم وسلوكهم المخالفين لعامة المنهج النبوي فلا يدخل في ذلك المذاهب الاجتهادية والجماعات الدعوية والمدارس العلمية والأحزاب السياسية، ولا يلزم أن يكون هذا التعدد والافتراق حاصلا في كل وقت من تاريخ الأمة بل المقصود أنه عند البعث يصل تعداد تلك الطوائف المنحرفة إلى هذا العدد الحاصل من الانحراف على طول تاريخ الأمة.

والله أعلم .

السؤال الثالث :

السلام عليكم و رحمة الله و بركاته إلى فضيلة الشيخ إننا مجموعة من الطلاب العراقيين والأكراد ندرس في هندستان، في بعض المرات هناك فرق يوم في إعلان العيد . فهل يجب علينا أن نكون مع الهند أو مع العراق؟ فمثلا اننا نقبل على عيد الأضحى فهل نكون معهم أو مع العراق أو مع السعودية كي لا يفوتنا صيام عرفة ؟ وجزاك الله خير الجزاء.

جواب السؤال الثالث :

أما بعد . إنما تصومون وتفطرون وتعيدون مع عامة مسلمي البلد الذي أنتم فيه فلا اعتبار للجنسيات في ذلك، كما أنكم لا يمكن أن تصلوا الصلوات الخمسة على حسب توقيت كردستان أو الحجاز وأنتم بالهند فكذلك لا تصومون بصومهم ولا تفطرون بفطرهم، وقد بوب الإمام النووي رحمه الله في شرحه لصحيح مسلم على حديث كريب فقال: ( باب بيان أن لكل بلد رؤيتهم)، ويوم عرفة هو اليوم التاسع من ذي الحجة بحسب الوقت والمكان الذي أنت فيه فيبدأ يوم عرفة في الهند بالضرورة قبل يوم عرفة بمكة بساعتين على الأقل وينتهي بغروب الشمس كذلك بالهند وإن كانت ساطعة على أهل صعيد عرفة . فالاعتبار لليوم التاسع من ذي الحجة لا لوقت وقوف الحجيج بعرفة.

والله أعلم .

السؤال الرابع :

ما حكم الشرع من العمل في البنك المركزي وخاصة وظيفة محلل مالي ؟!.

جواب السؤال الرابع:

الحمد لله والصلاة والسلام على رسول الله

أما بعد فإن البنك المركزي هو مثل غيره من مؤسسات الدولة والوزارات والإدارات وليس مثل البنوك التجارية الربوية فيجوز التوظف فيه في جميع إداراته ومصالحه ولا يجوز للموظف أن يمارس الربا أو أي أمر ممنوع شرعا في أية وظيفة كانت.

والله أعلم .
body_en:
As part of the "Fatwas" service offered by the scholarly website of his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, a number of varied questions reached the site's "mailbox", which his eminence the Sheikh answered in writing.

This set of questions takes in varied subjects, comprising questions on character and conduct, on transactions (muʿāmalāt) and economics, on the Islamic sects and groups, and on the rulings governing the sighting [of the new moon] for those resident outside their own countries.

The text of the questions and the answers:

The first question:

Peace be upon you, our Sheikh…

I know that backbiting is forbidden (ḥarām) and is among the major sins; but is it backbiting every time I want to ask after people and to know how they are, and whatever details that brings with it??

I have begun to be troubled by misgivings about this. And what of Aisha's account to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Umm Zarʿ, and the talk about those women's husbands, in terms of rulings??

I hope there is a ruling that will set my mind at rest and keep me from withdrawing from people altogether.

Answer to question 1)

The answer to the first question is that such misgivings are among the footsteps of Satan, which God has forbidden us to follow. God the Exalted said: {O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan; and whoever follows the footsteps of Satan — he commands indecency and wrong} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defined backbiting when he said: "It is your mentioning of your brother in terms he would dislike." So if a person is absent, and someone speaks at length about his honour

so as to diminish him and belittle him, that is the backbiting that God has forbidden — whether it relates to his physical make-up (khalq), or to his character (khuluq), or to anything else. Asking after how people are does not fall under it; but one who asks after people's circumstances should be moderate and confine himself to what concerns him, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Part of the excellence of a man's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him." The report of Umm Zarʿ that you mention is not of the category of backbiting, but of the category of unburdening oneself, the purpose of which is relief and consolation, as the poet said:

*One must complain to a man of chivalry, who will console you, or comfort you, or grieve with you.*

The people of knowledge have set out what is excepted from the prohibition of backbiting. They counted among it: what pertains to the appraisal of narrators (al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl) in transmission, and in giving sincere counsel; what its doer has himself done openly and proclaimed, of what is forbidden in the Sharia; what is said of the people of a country of what is widespread among them; and what two people discuss between themselves of what is already known to each of them.

And God knows best.

The second question: It is that I want to research the deviant schools, their branchings and their beliefs, in a simple and comprehensive way — what are the books that deal with that? And is the multiplicity of Islamic parties and groups, among them the Salafis, the Brotherhood and others, a good thing for the Ummah? And what is the way for the Ummah not to split into seventy-three sects? I hope my question is clear, and may God bless you.

The answer to the second question: The report about the Ummah's splitting has come down by several chains, not one of which is sound (ṣaḥīḥ). Some of the people of knowledge have graded it sound by reason of its chains, its corroborating routes and its supporting reports; but that does not establish the soundness of its several parts — it only makes it possible to establish the soundness of the core. So "all of them in the Fire except one", or "all of them in the Garden except one", or "whoever is upon the like of what I and my Companions are upon", are not sound. And supposing the core of the report to be sound, it is a report about a matter of the unseen, which one is under no obligation to strive to bring about. What is meant by it are the sects of those who deviate in their belief and their conduct, who depart from the prophetic way as a whole — so it does not take in the schools of legal reasoning, the groups working in daʿwah, the scholarly schools, or the political parties. Nor does it follow that this multiplicity and division should be present at every period of the Ummah's history; rather what is meant is that by the Resurrection the tally of those deviant factions reaches this number, arrived at from the deviation occurring across the whole length of the Ummah's history.

And God knows best.

The third question:

Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. To his eminence the Sheikh: we are a group of Iraqi and Kurdish students studying in Hindustan. Sometimes there is a day's difference in the announcement of the Eid. Are we obliged to be with India, or with Iraq? For example, we are approaching Eid al-Adha — are we to be with them, or with Iraq, or with Saudi Arabia, so that we do not miss the fast of ʿArafah? And may God reward you with the best of rewards.

The answer to the third question:

To proceed. You fast, and break your fast, and keep the Eid with the general body of the Muslims of the country you are in; nationality is of no account in this. Just as you cannot pray the five prayers according to the timings of Kurdistan or of the Hijaz while you are in India, so likewise you do not fast with their fasting, nor break your fast with their breaking of it. Imam al-Nawawi, may God have mercy on him, in his commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, headed the chapter on the report of Kurayb: "Chapter making clear that every land has its own sighting." And the day of ʿArafah is the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah according to the time and the place you are in. So the day of ʿArafah begins in India, necessarily, at least two hours before the day of ʿArafah in Mecca, and it likewise ends with the setting of the sun in India, even if the sun is still shining upon the people standing on the plain of ʿArafah. What counts is the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, not the time of the pilgrims' standing at ʿArafah.

And God knows best.

The fourth question:

What is the ruling of the Sharia on working in the central bank, and in particular in the post of financial analyst?!

The answer to the fourth question:

Praise be to God, and blessings and peace upon the Messenger of God.

To proceed: the central bank is like any other of the institutions of the state, the ministries and the administrations, and is not like the usurious commercial banks. So it is permissible to take employment in it, in all of its departments and services; and it is not permissible for an employee to engage in usurious gain (ribā), or in any matter forbidden in the Sharia, in any post whatsoever.

And God knows best.

flags.arabic: حديث افتراق الأمة قد ورد من طرق متعددة لا تصح منها واحدة … فلا يصح ( كلها في النار إلا واحدة) أو ( كلها في الجنة إلا واحدة) أو ( من كان على مثل ما أنا عليه أنا وأصحابي)
flags.context: the whole of the answer to the second question
options: not one of which is sound (ṣaḥīḥ) — a grading of the chains, individually
none of which is authentic
none of which is established
flags.note: HIGHEST-PRECISION PASSAGE IN THIS RECORD. The Sheikh is doing three separate things and the English must keep them apart: (1) he grades every individual chain of the 'seventy-three sects' report as not sound; (2) he concedes that some scholars grade the report sound in aggregate, but holds that this establishes only the core, not the famous additions, which he names and declares unsound; (3) even granting the core, he reads it as a report about the unseen, not a command, and expressly excludes the schools of law, the daʿwah groups, the scholarly schools and the political parties from its scope. ṣaḥīḥ is rendered 'sound' throughout, per the glossary, since this is hadith grading and not validity of an act. No grading has been added or dropped, and the concessive structure ('some have graded it sound ... but') must not be flattened in any excerpt, or the Sheikh will be made to say the opposite of what he says.

flags.arabic: وهل كثرة الأحزاب والجماعات الإسلامية ومنها السلفية والاخوان وغيرها خيرا للأمة ؟
options: translate the questioner's naming of the groups as it stands
generalise the named groups
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The named groups are the QUESTIONER's, and appear in a question about 'the deviant schools' and the seventy-three sects. The Sheikh's answer does the opposite of endorsing that framing — he expressly excludes daʿwah groups and political parties from the report's scope, and does not name or judge any group. In English, out of context, a heading pairing 'deviant sects' with the Salafis and the Muslim Brotherhood is readily clipped into something the Sheikh did not say, and the second of those is a proscribed organisation in several jurisdictions. Translated faithfully, with the attribution to the questioner kept visible; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: فيجوز التوظف فيه في جميع إداراته ومصالحه ولا يجوز للموظف أن يمارس الربا
flags.context: the ruling in the fourth answer
options: it is permissible to take employment in it … and it is not permissible for an employee to engage in usurious gain (ribā)
employment in it is allowed … and an employee may not deal in interest
flags.note: EDITORIAL and RULING-WORD. يجوز / لا يجوز is the legal 'permissible / not permissible', not the kalām modality of addendum section 8; the subject is an act. ribā is rendered 'usurious gain' per the glossary, NOT 'interest' — the category is wider, and the difference matters here, because the fatwa turns on a distinction between a central bank as an organ of state and a usurious commercial bank. Note that the ruling is conditional in its second half: permission to be employed does not extend to performing ribā-based work in any post. Both halves must appear together. A reader may take this as guidance on taking a specific job; it is a considered legal opinion (fatwā), non-binding, about a category of institution, given for a questioner in 2013.

flags.arabic: إنما تصومون وتفطرون وتعيدون مع عامة مسلمي البلد الذي أنتم فيه … فالاعتبار لليوم التاسع من ذي الحجة لا لوقت وقوف الحجيج بعرفة
flags.context: the answer to the third question, on moon-sighting and the fast of ʿArafah abroad
options: local sighting: one follows the country one is in, and the day of ʿArafah is the local ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah
one follows the sighting of Mecca
one follows one's country of origin
flags.note: A complete and unusually clear ruling on a question Muslims abroad ask constantly, and one on which the schools differ. The Sheikh gives the local-sighting position, cites al-Nawawi's chapter heading on the report of Kurayb for it, and applies it to the fast of ʿArafah specifically — which is the contested part, since many hold the fast to follow the pilgrims' standing. He does NOT report the contrary position here, and the English must not supply one. His reasoning that ʿArafah begins in India some hours before it begins in Mecca is correct as to the direction of the time difference and is reproduced as given.

flags.arabic: السلام عليكم شخنا .... / نص الأسئلة والاجوبة : / بالنسبة المقيمين في غير بلادهم
options: reproduce the source's spellings in body_ar and translate by the evident sense
correct them
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS (house rule 11), all orthographic and none affecting sense: شخنا for شيخنا; الاجوبة and ام and اننا and الاخوان without hamzah; بالنسبة المقيمين for بالنسبة للمقيمين; خيرا where the syntax calls for خير. The first answer also breaks to a new paragraph in the middle of a sentence (after فاستطال في عرضه), which body_ar and body_en both preserve. Nothing has been silently repaired.

flags.arabic: فلا بد من شكوى إلى ذي مروءة * يواسيك أو يسليك أو يتوجع.
flags.context: the line of verse in the first answer
options: One must complain to a man of chivalry, who will console you, or comfort you, or grieve with you
There is no escape from complaining to a man of honour, who consoles you, or distracts you, or feels your pain
flags.note: A line of nazm quoted from memory, with no poet named. Rendered as prose in italics per style guide section 4; no rhymed English attempted. مروءة is the classical virtue of manliness, honour and decency; 'chivalry' is the least misleading single word but is imperfect. يتوجع is 'feels pain on your behalf'.

flags.arabic: ( هي ذكرك أخاك بما يكره) … ( من حسن إسلام المرء تركه ما لا يعنيه) … ( باب بيان أن لكل بلد رؤيتهم)
flags.context: the reports and the chapter heading quoted in answers one and three
options: reproduce each quotation with only the attribution the Sheikh gives
supply collections and gradings
flags.note: The first two are prophetic reports given with no collection and no grading; the third is al-Nawawi's chapter heading, which the Sheikh does attribute and which the English attributes exactly as he does. No grading has been added to the first two, per style guide section 4.

flags.arabic: ندرس في هندستان … فهل يجب علينا أن نكون مع الهند
flags.context: the third questioner's description of where he is
options: studying in Hindustan (the questioner's word), with India in the following sentences
studying in India throughout
flags.note: The questioner writes هندستان, the Persianate name, then الهند in the next sentence; the Sheikh answers with الهند. The English keeps the questioner's 'Hindustan' where he uses it and 'India' elsewhere, rather than levelling the two, since the questioner is an Iraqi Kurd writing in his own register.

flags.arabic: عنوان الخبر عام بينما المتن أربع فتاوى كاملة
flags.context: the title and the CMS section of this record
options: record the CMS title and section as found, and type the item by its content
re-title and re-file it
flags.note: The CMS files this under 'news' with a generic headline, but the record carries four complete written fatwas, each with its questioner's text and the Sheikh's own answer, each closing with 'And God knows best'. Typed 'fatwa'; section and title recorded as found. Not re-filed unilaterally. The site should make the four questions individually findable — they are on backbiting, the seventy-three sects report, moon-sighting abroad, and employment in a central bank, and nothing in the headline says so.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: Four separate fatwas in one record. Each is translated in full; none is summarised.
الغيبة is rendered 'backbiting' throughout, the settled English term. The Prophet's definition is given as the Sheikh gives it.

بخلْق أو خُلُق: the source vocalises both words precisely in order to distinguish them — khalq, physical make-up, from khuluq, character. The English keeps both, with the Arabic, because the distinction is the whole point of the clause.

حديث أم زرع is the long report in which Aisha relates the talk of eleven women about their husbands; the questioner cites it as a possible counter-example to the prohibition of backbiting, and the Sheikh answers that it is unburdening rather than backbiting.

المذاهب الضالة in the questioner's words is rendered 'the deviant schools' and المذاهب الاجتهادية in the Sheikh's answer 'the schools of legal reasoning'; the same word مذاهب is doing different work in the two mouths and the English distinguishes them.

خبر عن أمر غيبي لا يلزم السعي لتحصيله: 'a report about a matter of the unseen, which one is under no obligation to strive to bring about' — the Sheikh's point being that a prediction of division is not an instruction to divide.
وقوف الحجيج بعرفة is the standing at ʿArafah, the essential element (rukn) of the hajj; rendered plainly rather than transliterated.
